user.title: Data sources
user.description: Sensors for the battery and prices. The energy statistics are prefilled from the Energy Dashboard. Remove duplicates, for example two grid sources that measure the same meter. House load is computed as import − export + solar + battery discharge − battery charge.

data.price_entity: Electricity price sensor (with today/tomorrow price attributes)
data.wholesale_source: Wholesale price history (for prices not yet published)

data.wear_cost: Battery wear cost per kWh throughput

tariff.title: Tariff
tariff.description: Prices for hours not yet published are estimated as a × wholesale + b. While net metering applies, export is paid at the import price. Otherwise export is paid as export a × wholesale + export b.

data.tariff_b: Import b (energy tax + markup, incl. VAT)
data.net_metering: Net metering (export paid at import price)

modes.title: Battery modes
modes.description: Tick the modes your system can do; Vulpes plans only with these. With grid setpoint (Victron ESS-style), charging holds grid import at the charge power and discharging holds grid export at the discharge power; with battery power, the battery itself runs at that power. Optionally pick the entity your current automation uses (for example an input_select) to compare the plan with what the house does.

data.power_control: How charge and discharge power is set
data.hold: Hold (charge from solar surplus only, never discharge)
data.self_consume: Self-consume (battery keeps the grid at zero)
data.pv_curtail: Solar can be switched off (for negative prices)
data.mode_entity: Compare with an existing mode entity (optional)

compare.title: Compare with {entity}
compare.description: For each Vulpes mode, choose the state of {entity} that means the same. Leave empty if there is none; that state then counts as disagreeing with the plan.

data.hold: Hold (charge from solar only, no discharge)

solar.title: Solar arrays
solar.description: Describe your solar panels. Rough values are fine: calibration refines them from your history.{calibration}

menu_options.solar_json: Paste plane JSON (advanced: microinverters, several inverters)

solar_system.title: Solar inverter
solar_system.description: Group your panels into arrays: panels with the same direction and tilt. All arrays share one inverter. After setup, Vulpes compares these values with your solar history and proposes corrections: it does so once by itself, and any time you press **Calibrate solar** on the Vulpes EMS device. Map each array's string power sensor for the best result. Apply the result under Configure → Solar arrays.

data_description.array_count: Usually one per roof side, or one per inverter input (MPPT).
data_description.inverter_ac_w: The maximum AC output on the inverter's data sheet. For a hybrid inverter with a battery on the DC side, use the maximum PV input power instead: solar can then exceed the AC output while it charges the battery.

solar_array.title: Solar array {index} of {count}
solar_array.description: Rough values are fine; calibration corrects them later.

data_description.direction: Pick a compass direction or type degrees clockwise from north (180 = south).
data_description.kwp: Number of panels × watt-peak per panel, in kWp.
data_description.power_entity: The inverter's DC power sensor for the input (MPPT) this array is connected to. With it, calibration can fit this array's direction and tilt; without it, only the total size is corrected.

solar_json.title: Solar planes (JSON)
solar_json.description: Paste a JSON list of planes (azimuth, tilt, pdc0 in W, ac_max in W, optionally inverter), or the output of `vulpes-cli calibrate-solar`.

error.invalid_planes: Invalid planes JSON: each plane needs azimuth, tilt, pdc0 and ac_max.
error.invalid_direction: Pick a direction, or enter degrees between 0 and 360.

abort.no_mode_options: The selected mode entity has no options.
